claims.claim_text: The indexed Nick J. Amigdalitis is strongly matched to Nick J. Amigdalitsis, a Technician Fifth Grade in the OSS Greek Operational Group.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An OSS Operational Groups roster places Nick J. Amigdalitsis in Greek Group IV; an independent memorial record repeats the name, grade, unit, and OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the very uncommon name, middle initial, Technician Fifth Grade, and explicit OSS Greek Operational Group assignment align across two independent specialist sources and the NARA index.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both corroborative sources concern his wartime OSS assignment. They do not establish a pre-OSS employer or immediate predecessor affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The index spelling Amigdalitis and the corroborative Amigdalitsis form are both preserved. The project does not silently choose one spelling or infer a pre-OSS Greek Battalion chronology from unit-level background alone.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified NARA row supplies the common name Ruth Ames, civilian grade CAF-5, and Box 13. Exact-name OSS, archival, newspaper, directory, obituary, and employment searches returned multiple uncorroborated namesakes and no source with two identifiers beyond the name.

person_updates.identity_evidence: A specialist OSS roster names a Sergeant Paul Amico in the Italian Operational Group's Fourth Group, matching the common indexed name and grade. A separately documented Secaucus Paul Amico entered the Army in 1944 and later held staff-sergeant rank, but neither his official Congressional tribute nor obituary supplies an OSS link or unique identifier. The candidates are not merged.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 13 and official Army records to determine whether the indexed Paul Amico served in the Italian Operational Group and whether the Secaucus candidate is the same person. Do not publish the diner chronology without a unique linkage. No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
